# WO-2026-08-12-B15-VISION-05 — Round 5: wire source_region through for real

## Acceptance criteria

AC1 (= acceptance_property): Fix `interpretPhotoOrchestrator.js:205-211` (or wherever the actual
projection lives once you read it fresh — Asdair's line numbers are from round 4's commit, confirm
against your own current read) so `source_region` survives the function's own return value. Trace
forward through `deps.js:realInterpretPhoto` and `runPipeline.js:stepInterpret`'s `readings` mapping —
Asdair confirmed both of those already expect the field, they just never receive it. Do not add a new
parallel field; make the existing one actually carry the value all the way through.

AC2: **Prove it with an integration-level test, not a fixture that can bypass the break.** Write a test
that exercises the REAL chain — `interpretPhotoWithDeps` (or the real production entry point) through to
`resolveByCatalogue.js`'s `resolveAll` — using a mocked vision-model response shaped like the actual
captured Lenor/Febreze collision (two lines, different regions, same `matched_regular_id`), and assert
both end up `needs_confirmation`. **This is the acceptance_property. Round 4's own test passed 6/6 by
calling `resolveAll` directly with hand-built fixtures already carrying `source_region` — that pattern
proved nothing about the real path and must not be the only proof again.**

AC3: Confirm, by reading the code path yourself before writing anything (not by trusting round 4's
report), exactly why round 4's own test didn't catch this — name the specific gap in your final report
so a future round doesn't reintroduce a fixture-only proof for a wiring-shaped defect.

AC4: Re-run the existing same-region and no-region auto-collapse tests (round 4's own coverage) to
confirm they still pass once real `source_region` values are flowing — this fix could plausibly change
their behaviour if any existing test accidentally relied on the null-everywhere state.

AC5: All touched-package tests pass with a non-zero executed count, including DB-gated tests via the
established disposable-Postgres pattern.
